subject: SlipWatch: MAP trigger — reprofile & exec gating
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 May 2024 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SlipWatch: MAP trigger — reprofile & exec gating

Team — quick note on Cobalt (COB-4921). During today's MAP checkpoint we got a firm procurement hold: they need an additional security attestation and a two-week procurement window for legal redlines. That pushes our current go-live target out. Immediate impacts:
- Acceptance window slips by ~3 weeks unless we compress testing.
- Procurement is insisting on contract language for data residency and audit logs (they flagged SOC2 artifact gaps).

Attached: initial reprofile (Cobalt_MAP_v4.pdf) and a draft SLA exception request. Proposed next steps:
1) Propose a revised MAP with explicit gated milestones (we own dev cut & feature freeze dates).
2) Offer a limited-production canary (non-sensitive dataset) to hold the acceptance window.
3) Request an exec-level procurement exception / credit if the delay extends beyond 30 days.

Can Marissa own the canary plan? Ben, can you size the cost/credit ask quickly so I can loop in sales leadership? Aditya, loop in security for the attestation gap — need ETA on artifacts. I’ll send the customer a short rebaseline note and ask for dates.

-Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Cobalt_MAP_v4.pdf (MAP draft, proposed dates), SLA-exception-request.docx (draft credit/SLA ask)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobaltanl.com>, Procurement <procurement@cobaltanl.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 May 2024 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed MAP rebaseline and canary option (Cobalt)

Hi Samir — thanks for the checkpoint this morning. I wanted to follow up with a concise proposal so procurement and your engineering leads can align. Summary: procurement hold for legal attestation will likely move our original go-live; rather than an open-ended delay we’re proposing a revised mutual action plan (attached) and a limited-production canary to preserve momentum.

Key asks from you:
- Confirm if procurement can provide a target date range for contract review completion (example: by 2024-06-18).
- If approval will be >3 weeks, would you accept a canary go-live on a non-PHI dataset to validate infra, observability, and runtime SLOs?

What we propose (Cobalt_MAP_v4.pdf):
- Week 0–2: legal review & artifact delivery (your procurement + our legal).
- Week 2–4: canary deployment (limited traffic, observability validation).
- Week 4–6: acceptance tests & full cutover window (contingent on signoffs).

If this timeline works, please reply with the procurement target date and any constraints for the canary (data slice, traffic cap). If procurement prefers a single go/no-go on full acceptance, we’ll put together an executive escalation runbook and a credit/SLA ask for extended delay.

Apologies for the bluntness — want to close the loop before the acceptance window widens. I’m available for a 30-min call if that helps.

Thanks —
Rachel

Attachment: Cobalt_MAP_v4.pdf

---
Note: internal recipients — Marissa will draft the canary plan; Ben to size the cost/credit ask; Aditya to chase security artifacts.

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobaltanl.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cobaltanl.com>, ahmed.khan@cobaltanl.com
Date: Fri, 10 May 2024 15:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP rebaseline and canary option (Cobalt)

Rachel — thanks for the clear framing. Procurement is stretched this cycle; current estimate is completion by 2024-06-20 (we'll try to tighten). Security audit artifacts: we can share SOC2 scoping notes and a subset of logs by next Tuesday, but full artifact package will take longer.

We are open to a canary on a limited dataset (non-PHI). Our constraints:
- Canary must only use anonymized telemetry and a synthetic sample (no production PII/PHI).
- Traffic capped at 5% of expected steady state.
- Must include a rollback plan and a telemetry snapshot shared daily.

If that fits your proposal, we can move forward with your Week 2 canary. If procurement is slower than 06/20, we will need a firm extension to the acceptance date and an update to the commercial terms (we'll discuss credits internally).

Regards,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Cobalt Analytics
samir.patel@cobaltanl.com
+1 (212) 555-0199

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: samir.patel@cobaltanl.com
Date: Sun, 12 May 2024 17:33:00 -07:00
Subject: ESCALATION: Cobalt procurement hold — exec ask and credit sizing (thread attached)

Team — forwarding Samir's reply (below). Procurement is giving 2024-06-20 as a realistic finish; they will accept a non-PHI canary with strict caps. Two immediate internal asks:
1) Marissa: build a 2-week canary runbook (data slice, rollback plan, monitoring report template). Target for me to share with Cobalt by EOD Tue.
2) Ben: draft the credit/SLA exception language. We should propose a pro-rated credit starting at day 31 of delay and a clear remediation path. Need a ballpark and the precedent (do we have similar credit language from previous deals?).

I’m elevating to sales leadership for approval on the credit ask and to legal for faster review of the SLA-exception. If sales leadership approves, we’ll present the exception as a conditional offer to preserve the acceptance window.

Quote:
> On Fri, 10 May 2024 at 15:26, Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobaltanl.com> wrote:
> Rachel — thanks for the clear framing. Procurement is stretched this cycle; current estimate is completion by 2024-06-20 (we'll try to tighten). Security audit artifacts: we can share SOC2 scoping notes and a subset of logs by next Tuesday, but full artifact package will take longer.
> 
> We are open to a canary on a limited dataset (non-PHI). Our constraints:
> - Canary must only use anonymized telemetry and a synthetic sample (no production PII/PHI).
> - Traffic capped at 5% of expected steady state.
> - Must include a rollback plan and a telemetry snapshot shared daily.

Action items summary (internal):
- Canopy/canary runbook (Marissa) — due 2024-05-14 17:00 PDT.
- Credit/SLA ask (Ben) — draft due 2024-05-13 12:00 PDT.
- Security artifacts chase (Aditya) — get SOC2 scoping notes by 2024-05-14.

I will schedule a quick 15-min sync with SalesLead to get alignment on the credit ceiling. If leadership prefers, we can present two options to the customer: (A) no-credit canary path to preserve acceptance window; (B) credit-backed acceptance path if procurement pushes beyond 06/20.

Thanks —
Rachel

[Attachment forwarded: Cobalt_MAP_v4.pdf]
